newsitem.title: USA: BT targets U.S. broadcast transmission market.
newsitem.headline: BT targets U.S. broadcast transmission market.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp formed an alliance to extend BT's existing broadcast video transmission business in Europe into the United States, the companies said Tuesday.

British Telecom's Broadcast Services unit, the leading provider of video broadcast services in Europe and over trans-Atlantic routes, said it planned to use MCI's network infrastructure to move rapidly into the U.S. market.
Film and video producers and network programmers use the services to deliver programming between production and broadcast facilities.
MCI previously was not active in broadcast services.
The U.S. market is now dominated by two players -- France Telecom's Globecast, and Williams Cos Inc's Vivx unit. It is estimated to be worth about $250 million a year, according to a BT official.

John Swingewood, the BT Broadcast unit's general manager, said in a telephone interview that the BT-MCI alliance aimed to become the No. 3 player within its first year in the U.S. market. "That clearly has to be the ambition," he said.
"In conjunction with MCI, we expect to tap into huge demand from the U.S. transmission market for both domestic and international broadcast services," he said.
BT's Broadcast Services unit has revenues of $300 million from existing European and transoceanic businesses, he said.

The BT-MCI alliance will offer competitive terrestrial and satellite transmission services within the United States and provide routes for sending and receiving global programming from Europe and the rest of the world.

Swingewood said the service was aimed at feeding the growing demand among European audiences for U.S. sports programming, especially basketball and football, and the interest in European news by American audiences.

He said the new alliance builds upon BT Broadcast Services' existing European network facilities in London, Paris, Brussels, Cologne and Moscow and adds four U.S.-based MCI sites to give customers true trans-Atlantic reach.

One service in the new video transmission suite is MediaVision, which will enable film and video production companies in Los Angeles, New York and London to collaborate on special effects and post-production work.

In addition, the BT-MCI alliance plans to offer an Internet-based online booking service that provides customers with one-stop shopping for end-to-end transmission services. Swingewood said that mechanism was unique in the industry.
"With a simple click of the mouse, broadcasters will be able to control the scheduling and switching of their video traffic globally," MCI said in a statement.
MCI and BT in 1996 agreed to merge to form Concert, a global communications company. The deal awaits U.S. Federal Communications Commission approval, which is expected by fall.
